clause: IAG Directors who undertake a Dealing in IAG Securities following consent must provide the Group Company Secretary within 1 business day of the execution of the trade a confirmation of trade so that an ASX Appendix 3Y can be completed and lodged with the ASX within 5 business days.
why_it_matters: A director's collar would become publicly disclosed on an Appendix 3Y within days of execution, which feeds back into the front page test at the consent stage.

clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities at any time, including in the exceptional circumstances referred to in section 6, unless the Restricted Person first obtains prior written clearance from [the Approving Officer].
why_it_matters: Clearance is required for every leg of a funded collar at any time of year, not just in Blackout Periods, so entry, roll, unwind and physical settlement each need a fresh written approval.

topic: secured lending is permitted with clearance
clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies with a flat ban, the loan leg secured on the collared shares is permissible here provided the Approving Officer gives prior written clearance, which makes a funded collar structurally available.

clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs over vested shares are a clearance decision rather than a prohibition, so the whole structure turns on the Chair's or Managing Director's willingness to approve.

clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
why_it_matters: Absolute with no clearance route, so the collar and any security must be confined to shares that have already vested and been delivered.

clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from the section 5 restrictions].
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale over the collared shares in a Blackout Period does not put the executive in breach, which removes the single biggest obstacle most ASX policies present to a funded collar.

clause: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for the period of five business days from the time which it is given or such other period as may be determined by the Approving Officer. The expiry time of the clearance will be stated in the clearance granted.
why_it_matters: The collar must be priced, documented and executed inside five business days unless the Approving Officer expressly extends the window in the clearance itself.

clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities within any period imposed by the Board from time to time ... Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed Board-imposed Additional Period can block execution or unwind of the collar at any time, and the executive cannot even tell the bank why.

clause: the end of each of the March and September financial quarters and 24 hours immediately following the release of the Company's quarterly reports for those financial quarters
why_it_matters: As a mining company PLS has four closed periods a year rather than two, materially narrowing the windows in which a collar can be struck or unwound.

clause: Restricted Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.
why_it_matters: Undefined, so a short-dated or knock-out collar risks being characterised as speculative; a multi-year tenor with no early termination triggers is safer.

clause: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise, (Company Securities)
why_it_matters: Both collar legs are themselves Company Securities, so acquiring the put and writing the call are separately 'trading' events needing clearance and falling outside Prohibited Periods.

clause: Where this policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act or thing, the relevant Restricted Person must do that act or thing in respect of the Connected Person.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or loan through a family trust, controlled company or spouse does not avoid the clearance requirement; the executive must procure compliance.

clause: Breach of this policy (irrespective of whether the insider trading prohibition or any other law is breached) will also be regarded by the Group as serious misconduct which may lead to disciplinary action and/or dismissal.
why_it_matters: Executing any collar leg without written clearance is a dismissal-level offence, so the bank should condition drawdown on sighting the clearance.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: Directors, KMPs and Employees are prohibited from using margin loans to finance the purchase of securities in the Company or from trading in any financial products issued or created over the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: both collar legs are financial products created over Company securities, so the derivative overlay is banned outright with no approval route, regardless of vesting state.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
topic: hedging ban is narrower than the products ban
clause: must not trade in securities of the Company ... as part of a hedging arrangement if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting their exposure to Company securities that have not vested or are subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: Section 10 alone would permit hedging fully vested unrestricted shares, so any argument for a collar must overcome section 11.1 rather than section 10.1.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: prohibited from using margin loans to finance the purchase of securities in the Company
why_it_matters: The financing ban bites only on borrowing to buy Company shares, so a bank loan secured on an existing vested holding is not expressly prohibited, leaving the derivative legs as the sole blocker.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: The policy contains no provision on granting security, charges, liens or pledges over Company securities, on forced sales by a secured lender, on margin calls, or on disclosure of encumbrances.
why_it_matters: A lender enforcing security during a Closed Period has no express carve-out, so the executive would have to rely on the general 'no control or influence' exclusion in section 8.1 with no certainty.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: This is the case even if clearance to trade securities has been granted under this policy. Such clearance is taken to be revoked if the relevant person seeking to trade is in possession of non-public price sensitive information about or affecting the relevant securities.
why_it_matters: Approval is automatically void on receipt of inside information, so any structure must be executed immediately after approval and cannot rely on a standing consent.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: The written approval shall have effect for a period of four weeks from the date of the approval notice or a shorter period if specified in the notice unless a material change in circumstances occurs. ... Written approval to trade during a Prohibited Period is discretionary, is not an endorsement of the proposed trade and can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: Even the generous four-week exceptional-circumstances approval is expressly revocable, so a bank cannot treat it as a committed condition precedent.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: A decision to refuse approval to trade during a Prohibited Period is final and binding and must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: There is no appeal and the executive cannot explain to the bank why a trade date was missed.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: This Policy applies to trading in the securities of Washington H. Soul Pattinson and Company Limited, those of its controlled and associated entities and those of entities in which it has a Substantial Interest [5% or more of the voting shares].
why_it_matters: A collar over shares in any listed investee in which SOL holds 5% or more also needs Chairman approval, which matters given SOL's investment portfolio.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: Sections 10.1 and 11.1 bind 'Directors, KMPs and Employees' whereas sections 2.2, 4.1, 5.1, 6.1 and 9.1 bind those persons 'and their Associates'.
why_it_matters: The drafting arguably leaves Associates outside the financial products ban, but the Associate definition and the approval requirement make any attempt to structure around it plainly against the policy's intent.

company: WASHINGTON H. SOUL PATTINSON AND COMPANY LIMITED
clause: A breach of this policy will be recorded, and serious breaches will be reported to the Leadership Team and the Board.
why_it_matters: Entering a collar without approval would be escalated to the Board rather than handled informally, with termination of employment expressly contemplated.

clause: The policy contains no clause prohibiting hedging. Instead, 'Other financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares' are simply included in the definition of SGH securities.
why_it_matters: This is the key enabling feature: a collar is regulated as an ordinary dealing needing a window or clearance, rather than banned, and there is no ban on hedging unvested or restricted plan securities either.

topic: absolute blackout ban on derivative products
clause: In addition, during the blackout periods, no Executives or designated staff may deal in financial products issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities. No exceptional circumstances exemption applies to this prohibition.
why_it_matters: Collar entry, roll, unwind or any adjustment involving the option legs is absolutely impossible in a blackout period, with no hardship or court-order relief, so the bank must build hard date constraints into the trade.

clause: Any designated employee must obtain clearance in writing from the relevant approver detailed in the table in Section 3 for any proposed dealing in SGH securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement. ... Clearance may be granted subject to any conditions the approver determines appropriate.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is permitted with clearance rather than prohibited, and the approver's power to impose conditions gives the company a way to protect itself rather than refuse outright.

clause: this policy does not apply to: ... A disposal of SGH securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a margin lending arrangement, where this policy has been complied with in relation to the margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: Lender enforcement over the collared shares, including in a blackout period, is outside the policy, but only if the underlying facility was itself properly cleared, so the bank should make clearance a condition precedent and retain evidence of it.

clause: Clearance may be given in any written form and is effective for two business days after it has been given.
why_it_matters: The collar and the loan must be documented in advance and executed within two business days of clearance, so pricing and legal work must be complete before the approval is sought.

clause: In the period between 24 hours and 30 working days after the release of SGH's Half Yearly Results announcement ... Annual Results announcements ... and the close of the SGHs Annual General Meeting.
why_it_matters: Three 30-working-day windows a year give ample scope to strike or unwind a collar without needing discretionary clearance at all.

clause: A designated employee must not be involved in a decision regarding their own application for clearance.
why_it_matters: For a Chairman or CEO collar the approval must come from the Lead Independent Director or ARC Chair, so the bank should verify who signed the clearance.

topic: no short-term or speculative trading rule
clause: The policy imposes no minimum holding period and no restriction on short-term or speculative dealing.
why_it_matters: Collar tenor is unconstrained by the policy, so short-dated or rolling structures are not objectionable on their face.

clause: Deal includes buying and selling, as well as procuring others to buy or sell.
why_it_matters: Granting security is not literally a Deal, so section 5 rather than the general definition is what brings the loan and any share transfer into the clearance net; a pledge unconnected to a lending arrangement sits in a gap.

clause: Associates of designated employees must comply with the policy as if they were a designated employee ... A breach of this policy, including a breach by an associate, will be regarded as serious misconduct.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar through a family trust or superannuation fund attracts the identical window, clearance and blackout constraints and the employee bears the consequences.

clause: All designated employees and their associates must obtain approval prior to trading in the securities of listed entities in which SGH has a Substantial Interest (including controlled and associated entities) [Appendix 1: Beach Energy (BPT), Boral (BLD), Seven West Media (SWM)].
why_it_matters: A collar over Beach Energy, Boral or Seven West Media shares held by an SGH designated employee also requires prior approval under this policy.

clause: The following transactions relating to trading in the Company's securities are excluded from the operation of this policy: ... a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights.
why_it_matters: This is the single most collar-friendly clause in the policy: the bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares, including a sale in a closed period, falls outside the policy altogether, so the executive does not breach by reason of the lender enforcing.

clause: The policy contains no margin lending, secured financing, pledge or encumbrance prohibition of any kind, and no disclosure obligation in respect of any such facility.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is unrestricted, which is unusual among ASX policies and removes the usual blocking provision.

clause: Directors and employees are prohibited from trading during prohibited periods in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs are financial products over Lynas securities, so entry, amendment, roll, unwind and any cash or physical settlement of the collar must all be timed to fall inside a three-week open window.

clause: All periods other than the periods referred to in paragraphs 7.1 and 9.2 are “closed periods” during which all directors and employees are generally prohibited from Dealing in Securities of the Company.
why_it_matters: Lynas is closed by default and open only for three weeks after results, the AGM or a prospectus, so there may be as little as four short windows a year in which a collar can be struck or unwound.

clause: clearance may be given by the Chairman and at least one other non-executive director for the director or employee to sell (but not to purchase) securities when he or she otherwise would not be permitted to do so.
why_it_matters: Out-of-window relief is confined to selling, so it cannot be used to buy back a written call, close out a put or enter a collar outside a window; only an outright sale of the underlying can be cleared.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested options
clause: Directors and employees must not at any time hedge options issued to them under an employee option plan prior to vesting of the options.
why_it_matters: The hedging prohibition is confined to unvested employee options, so a collar over vested shares is not caught by it, but unvested option entitlements must be excluded from the collared parcel.

clause: Directors and employees must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.
why_it_matters: With no defined holding period, a short-dated collar or one with early termination or roll features risks being characterised as short-term trading, so a long tenor and confirmation from the Chairman or Secretary at clearance are advisable.

clause: the Chairman or Secretary has indicated in writing that there is no impediment to them doing so; and the proposed Dealing is permitted under paragraph 7.1 or 9.2.
why_it_matters: The policy sets no window within which a cleared trade must be executed and no express revocation right, so the bank should document that the written no-impediment confirmation is current at pricing and at each subsequent leg.

clause: directors and employees should consider this policy to be binding on them in the absence of specific exemption by the board.
why_it_matters: The board can exempt a specific transaction from the policy entirely, which offers a route to sanction a collar whose timing or structure does not fit the narrow windows.

clause: This policy has been implemented to prevent the incidence of 'insider trading' ... by directors and employees and persons associated with any of them. ... a director or employee must not recommend or otherwise suggest to any person (including a spouse, relative, friend, trustee of a family trust or directors of a family company) that they buy or sell securities in the Company.
why_it_matters: Associates are referred to in the introduction but no associate is defined and no operative rule binds them, so a collar entered by a spouse or family trust sits in an untested area rather than a clearly permitted or prohibited one.

clause: Directors must notify the company secretary immediately on acquiring or disposing of a relevant interest in any securities in the Company.
why_it_matters: Entering the collar may change the director's relevant interest, or be treated as doing so on physical settlement, triggering immediate notice to the company secretary and an Appendix 3Y within 5 Business Days that will disclose the structure publicly.

clause: Directors and Designated Persons are not permitted at any time (including outside any Closed Period) to enter into any hedging instruments or arrangements regarding or derivative financial products issued over any APA Securities held by the Director or Designated Person.
why_it_matters: This single clause defeats the funded collar: both the purchased put and the written call are derivative financial products issued over APA Securities held by the executive, and the ban is absolute in time, indifferent to vesting, and has no clearance or exemption route.

clause: Directors and Designated Persons may include APA Securities in a diversified portfolio under a margin loan facility or secured financing arrangement provided that: the facility or arrangement does not permit title to the APA Securities to be transferred.
why_it_matters: Even setting the derivatives ban aside, the loan leg fails on its own terms: a facility secured solely on the collared APA parcel is not a diversified portfolio, and any title-transfer collateral or rehypothecation right is expressly prohibited, so only a non-title-transfer security interest inside a broader portfolio facility is permitted.

clause: Directors and Designated Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any APA Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that person, or any third party.
why_it_matters: Unvested and holding-locked securities are unavailable as collateral in any structure, and the words 'directly or indirectly' and 'or any third party' block back-to-back or guarantee arrangements over that stock.

clause: to avoid doubt, the terms of this policy will continue to apply to the relevant APA Securities, including the requirement that they not be disposed of in a Closed Period unless permission for such disposal is granted pursuant to section 4.2.7.
why_it_matters: A margin call or enforcement sale during a Closed Period is not an excluded dealing and requires exceptional circumstances permission from the Chairman, so a lender cannot rely on unfettered enforcement rights and the borrower bears the timing risk.

clause: Clearance to undertake a proposed dealing will be valid for three business days or until a Closed Period commences, whichever is the shorter period.
why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing in the underlying must be priced and executed within three business days, and a clearance may be withdrawn if circumstances change, which constrains any multi-leg execution.

clause: The decision to give or refuse clearance is in the absolute discretion of the Recipient and is final and binding on the Applicant, and reasons for the decision need not be provided. ... If clearance is refused, the Applicant must keep the fact of that refusal confidential.
why_it_matters: There is no appeal and no obligation to explain, and the executive cannot tell a bank counterparty why a transaction cannot proceed, so financing documents should not require disclosure of the reason for a refusal.

clause: the guiding principle is that Directors and Designated Persons who purchase APA Securities should intend, at the time of acquisition, to continue to hold the purchased APA Securities for at least the next 12 months.
why_it_matters: Any structure with an economic tenor of under 12 months, or that contemplates repurchasing securities delivered under the collar, risks being treated as short-term or speculative trading.

topic: same open period buy and sell
clause: Directors and Designated Persons must not both buy and sell APA Securities in the same “open” period between two consecutive Closed Periods.
why_it_matters: Physical settlement of a collar combined with any purchase in the same open window would breach this rule, so delivery and any repurchase must straddle a Closed Period.

clause: APA Group requires that Directors and Designated Persons take all reasonable steps to cause their respective Related Parties to comply with this section 4.2 as if they were Directors or Designated Persons.
why_it_matters: Holding the collared stock through a spouse, resident child, family trust, superannuation fund or significantly influenced company does not escape the hedging ban or the financing conditions.

clause: derivative financial products issued over any APA Securities held by the Director or Designated Person.
why_it_matters: The ban is drafted by reference to securities held, so a cash-settled index or basket derivative not referable to a held parcel is arguably outside 4.2.5, though it would still face the short selling and short-term trading prohibitions in 4.2.4.

clause: other persons specified from time to time by the Managing Director ... The Company Secretary will operate a process for regularly reviewing the list of Designated Persons and maintain a register of Designated Persons, and will notify relevant individuals of their inclusion on or removal from the register.
why_it_matters: An executive outside section 4.2 today can be brought within it at the Managing Director's discretion, so any structure entered by a non-Designated employee should be documented to survive, or be unwound on, later designation.

clause: If it becomes apparent that a Director has breached this policy, APA Group will give careful consideration to whether it ought to make an announcement to the market explaining the circumstances of the breach and what, if any, remedial and/or disciplinary action it has taken.
why_it_matters: A breach by a Director carries express reputational exposure through a possible market announcement, raising the stakes on any structure that sits close to the 4.2.5 line.

clause: You must not engage in transactions in the derivative markets involving products based on Xero Securities. This includes OTC products ... caps and collars and any other financial product that operates to limit the economic risk associated with Xero Securities.
why_it_matters: This is one of the few ASX policies that names 'collars' and 'OTC products' expressly, so the derivative legs of a funded collar are prohibited on their face rather than merely caught by a definition.

topic: exceptional circumstances as the only derivatives gate
clause: You may apply for approval to enter into one of these transactions in exceptional circumstances. Approval will not be given in relation to unvested Xero Securities.
why_it_matters: A collar over vested shares is not absolutely barred, but it can only proceed through an exceptional-circumstances application (severe hardship, court order or similar), which a commercial monetisation is unlikely to satisfy.

clause: Whether or not you are a Designated Person, you must seek clearance ... before you: enter into a margin loan or other secured financing arrangements (including transferring Xero Securities into an existing margin loan account); grant a security or rights over your Xero Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan and security legs of a funded collar are permitted with clearance, so the structure fails only on the derivative legs; a plain secured loan against Xero shares without a hedge is available.

clause: You must not enter into an arrangement or transaction that ... otherwise enables you to profit from a decrease in the market price of Xero Securities.
why_it_matters: This limb is not restricted to unvested holdings and independently catches the purchased put in a collar over fully vested shares.

clause: Xero takes a 'substance over form' approach and has regard to the intent and spirit of this policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: Structuring around the derivatives ban (for example a non-recourse loan with an economically equivalent payoff, or a hedge booked at a Connected Person entity) will be assessed on its economic substance.

clause: Where clearance is required to deal under this policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not meet the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even the permitted secured financing leg can be refused on reputational grounds alone, without reasons being given.

clause: They may also decide to impose conditions on the dealing or withdraw the clearance at any time. If your clearance is not approved or is withdrawn, you must keep this fact confidential. Clearance is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if you become aware of Inside Information prior to dealing.
why_it_matters: A bank cannot rely on a granted clearance surviving to signing or drawdown; it can be withdrawn at any time or lapse automatically, and the executive cannot explain why.

clause: Your Connected Persons should only deal in Xero Securities in circumstances where you yourself would be permitted to do so. Where clearance requirements would apply to your dealing, you must comply with those requirements on behalf of your Connected Persons.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan in a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the derivatives ban or the clearance obligation.

clause: Short term dealing is the buying and selling of listed securities within a 6 month period.
why_it_matters: A collar with a tenor under six months, or one whose entry and physical settlement fall within six months, risks characterisation as short-term dealing on top of the derivatives ban.

topic: no venue limitation and no vesting limitation on the derivatives ban
clause: any other financial product that operates to limit the economic risk associated with Xero Securities
why_it_matters: Unlike venue-limited bans elsewhere, this catch-all covers OTC bank-written puts and calls over on-market as well as plan-sourced shares.

clause: For Nominated Qantas Employees, the definition of Dealing is further extended to prohibit: (a) hedging or otherwise entering into a contract with the purpose of securing a profit or avoiding a loss by reference to fluctuations in the price of the Securities of Qantas ...; and (b) any margin lending or securities lending arrangement, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance ... where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost.
why_it_matters: This single paragraph blocks both legs of a funded collar for directors and executives, and its drafting is ambiguous between a flat ban and an enlargement of Dealing that would leave both legs available with a written Request to Deal outside Closed Periods; the point should be settled with the Company Secretary before any structuring work.

topic: loss of control of sale process
clause: where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost
why_it_matters: The financing prohibition is qualified, so a facility in which the bank has no independent power of sale (for example, cash-settled legs, a non-recourse structure with no enforcement right over the shares, or security requiring the executive to direct any sale) may fall outside 3.45(b) even though a conventional margin loan does not.

topic: set off and withholding rights are encumbrances
clause: including a mortgage, charge, pledge, lien or title retention arrangement, right of set off or right to withhold payment of a deposit or other money, or any third party interest such as a trust or an equity
why_it_matters: Ordinary bank documentation terms such as set-off and the right to withhold a cash collateral deposit are themselves prohibited encumbrances, so even a lightly secured collar loan is caught.

clause: may be given clearance to Deal as outlined in paragraphs 3.44 and 3.46, except in relation to Securities that are unvested
why_it_matters: Unvested plan securities can never be hedged, pledged or dealt with, even in severe financial hardship, so the collateral and hedge pool is limited to vested, unrestricted shares.

clause: this paragraph does not permit the Nominated Qantas Employee to otherwise Deal in those Restricted Securities
why_it_matters: Shares that have vested but remain subject to plan restrictions are also outside the collar pool.

clause: The approval is valid for one month unless another period is agreed by the Chairman or CEO.
why_it_matters: Any exceptional-circumstances clearance gives a generous one-month execution window compared with the two to five business days common elsewhere, which would comfortably accommodate collar documentation and pricing if such a clearance could be obtained.

clause: “Securities” means shares, options or other securities or derivatives (including any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, contract for difference, spread bet, warrant or depository receipt) issued by any listed entity or issued or created over the listed entity's securities by third parties.
why_it_matters: Bank-written OTC options over Qantas shares are Securities with no venue limitation, so entering the collar is a Dealing in its own right and not merely a hedge.

clause: any family member or associate over whom they have influence, including specifically any person who lives in the same home as the Nominated Qantas Employee
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a spouse, household member or influenced entity does not escape the paragraph 3.44 and 3.45 restrictions.

clause: Nominated Qantas Employees means Directors, Company Secretaries, Executive Management Members, direct reports to Executive Management Members, and other Executives specifically notified by the CEO or his nominee from time to time.
why_it_matters: Employees below direct reports to Executive Management Members are outside the hedging, margin lending and encumbrance prohibitions entirely and face only the statutory insider trading rule, but they are also unlikely to be the bank's target clients.

clause: Last updated (version) 28 August 2013
why_it_matters: This is the version lodged under Listing Rule 12.10 in September 2013; a current version should be obtained from the Company Secretary before relying on the analysis, as the hedging and financing paragraphs may have changed.

topic: collar named as restricted trading, not prohibited
clause: entering into any other form of derivative contract relating to a security, such as a cap or collar facility; and any other transaction that limits the economic risk of holding a security.
why_it_matters: BlueScope names a collar facility in the list of what counts as trading rather than in a prohibition, so the derivative legs of a collar over vested unrestricted shares are available to a Restricted Person inside a trading window with written clearance.

clause: From the date this section takes effect, Restricted Persons must not enter into any new arrangements under which their BlueScope Steel securities are pledged as collateral for a loan or other agreement which could permit a sale of those securities without the security holder's consent.
why_it_matters: This defeats the funded leg of a conventional collar loan, because a bank's security over the collared shares almost always includes an enforcement power of sale that does not require the holder's consent.

clause: which could permit a sale of those securities without the security holder's consent
why_it_matters: The prohibition is conditional, so a facility with no independent power of sale (cash settlement only, or security requiring the executive to direct any disposal) may fall outside it, and this is the drafting point to negotiate.

clause: Exceptions will not be considered in the case of trading resulting from a forced sale in breach of this policy.
why_it_matters: If a bank ever enforced, the executive would be in breach with no available cure, and breach is expressly a disciplinary matter that may include termination.

clause: any dealing in the same BlueScope Steel securities within a 9 month period is prohibited
why_it_matters: One of the longest short-term bans in the market: a collar over recently acquired shares, or one whose physical settlement occurs within nine months of the underlying purchase, would breach it, so tenor must exceed nine months and the underlying shares must be seasoned.

clause: the 45 day periods from the commencement of trading the day following the announcement of the half year results and the day following the announcement of the full year results; and the 15 day period from the commencement of the trading day following the Annual General Meeting.
why_it_matters: Restricted Persons may deal only inside roughly 105 days a year, so collar entry, any roll and any physical settlement must all be scheduled into a window, and the Board may narrow a window before it opens.

topic: ten trading day clearance with revocation
clause: The approval to trade in BlueScope Steel securities is valid for 10 trading days from the time the approval is given, and may be revoked at any time.
why_it_matters: A comparatively long execution window for documenting and pricing a collar, but the bank cannot treat clearance as irrevocable up to signing.

clause: if a genuine and pressing requirement for funds causes a need to sell BlueScope Steel securities, then exceptions may be considered
why_it_matters: Out-of-window relief is framed around a need to sell, so it is doubtful the Chairman could use it to authorise entry into a collar or a financing outside a window.

clause: Employees who hold unvested or restricted BlueScope Steel securities must ... not enter any transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested or restricted securities.
why_it_matters: The hedgeable pool is limited to shares that have vested and whose restriction period has ended; this ban applies to every employee, not only Restricted Persons, and has no clearance route.

clause: An employee or director must ensure that any Controlled Entity ... does not trade in BlueScope Steel securities except in accordance with this Policy (and as if the Controlled Entity itself was a Restricted Person).
why_it_matters: A family trust or investment company used to hold the collared shares is treated as a Restricted Person in its own right, so the window, clearance and pledging rules follow the shares.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested and locked securities
clause: Company securities acquired under an employee or director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting. Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee or director equity plan operated by the Company.
why_it_matters: The hedging section is drafted as two targeted prohibitions rather than a general ban, so hedging vested unrestricted shares is left permitted and the derivative legs of a collar over those shares are available.

topic: secured lender enforcement is an excluded dealing
clause: Sections 4.2, 5.1, 5.3 and 5.4 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: This is the most bank-friendly clause in the policy: enforcement by the lender, even in a blackout period, is expressly carved out of the short-term trading ban, the blackout and the notification and approval requirements, so the executive is not put in breach by the bank's own sale.

clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with section 5.6(a) conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: The Company can dictate the enforcement mechanics of the facility as a condition of approving it, so the bank should expect the loan documentation to be negotiated with the Company Secretary rather than approved as presented.

topic: directors notify rather than seek approval
clause: a Director may deal at any time for a period of 5 business days following notification. By notifying their intention to deal, the Director is taken to have satisfied themselves that the proposed dealing is within the terms of this Securities Trading Policy.
why_it_matters: Directors self-certify for ordinary dealings, giving a clean 5 business day execution window with no approval risk; note that this route does not extend to margin lending, which needs approval under section 5.6 regardless of tier.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: A collar that in substance hedges unvested or locked plan securities, even if written over an equal number of unrestricted shares, would be treated as breaching section 4.3, and a bespoke loan secured on shares should be cleared as if it were a margin lending arrangement.

clause: The policy names only 'a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities' and 'transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account' as financing triggers.
why_it_matters: There is no general prohibition on granting security over Company securities and no financier disclosure regime, so the funding leg of a collar is unobstructed on the face of the policy.

topic: forward contracts as short term dealings
clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 6 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: The tenor of the collar and of any forward element must exceed six months, and the collared shares should not have been bought on market within the preceding six months.

clause: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities if ... the Company has notified Employees that they must not deal in securities (either for a specified period, or until the Company gives further notice).
why_it_matters: An open-ended notice can be issued to all Employees at any time and would block collar entry, unwind or physical settlement without any stated end date.

clause: The Policy refers throughout to 'the Company's securities' without defining the term and contains no derivatives or securities definition.
why_it_matters: It is arguable that a bank-written OTC option is not itself one of 'the Company's securities', so the notification and approval regime may not formally bite on the derivative legs; the prudent course is to notify or clear them anyway given the substance over form clause.

clause: A request for approval to deal will be answered as soon as practicable and typically within one business day.
why_it_matters: An unusually fast and explicit service level, which makes it practical to align clearance with pricing on a specific trade date.

topic: standing ban on all associated financial products
clause: A Restricted Employee must not ... deal at any time in financial products associated with Medibank Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted under this policy.
why_it_matters: This is the clause that defeats the collar: it is unqualified as to vesting state and venue, and the only carve-out is the closed list of section 5 Permitted Dealings, none of which is a derivative.

clause: For the purposes of this section, financial products include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Medibank Securities by third parties.
why_it_matters: Third-party created OTC instruments are expressly within scope, so a bank-written put and call over Medibank shares cannot be argued outside the prohibition on the basis that they are not exchange traded.

clause: In addition, Restricted Employees must not, without the consent of the Company Secretary, enter into any other funding arrangements where Medibank Securities may be included as security (for example any lending arrangement that involves the Restricted Employee granting an 'all assets' security interest to secure the repayment of a loan).
why_it_matters: The funding leg of a collar is available with Company Secretary consent, so a plain loan secured on Medibank shares is possible even though the hedge is not.

topic: consented lender enforcement is a permitted dealing
clause: (lender disposal) a disposal of Medibank Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement or other funding arrangements, where such arrangements are prohibited by this policy
why_it_matters: Enforcement by a bank under a facility consented to under 6.1(b) is excluded from the Blackout Periods and the notification process, but enforcement under any facility the policy prohibits is not protected, which makes obtaining the Company Secretary's consent the single most important condition precedent.

clause: Restricted Employees should consult the Relevant Notification Officer if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: Whether a collar loan is a prohibited margin lending arrangement or a consentable 6.1(b) funding arrangement is decided by the company, not the bank, so the classification should be confirmed in writing before the facility is documented.

clause: A Restricted Employee may request, and the Relevant Notification Officer may give, prior confirmation for the Restricted Employee to: (a) deal in Medibank Securities during a Blackout Period; or (b) dispose of Medibank Securities even if otherwise prohibited under section 6
why_it_matters: The only relief from section 6 is a disposal, so no exceptional circumstance, however severe, can authorise entering a hedge, derivative or prohibited financing.

topic: ninety day hold applies to the derivative itself
clause: Restricted Employees must hold any Medibank Securities or financial products associated with Medibank Securities for at least 90 days.
why_it_matters: Even if the derivative ban were relaxed, the collar position itself would have to be held for at least 90 days, ruling out short-dated or early-terminable structures.

clause: "Medibank Securities" means Securities of, or whose value is materially determined by reference to, Medibank.
why_it_matters: Instruments whose value tracks the Medibank share price are Medibank Securities in their own right, so the clearance, blackout and 90 day holding rules attach to them directly and not only through the section 6 prohibition; note the general Securities definition is limited to products 'able to be traded on a financial market', a tension the section 6.4 definition overrides for section 6 purposes.

clause: companies with which the Restricted Employee is connected by directly or indirectly: (i) holding at least 20% of the share capital; or (ii) controlling the exercise of at least 20% of the voting power ... a trustee where the beneficiaries of the trust include the Restricted Employee or his or her spouse, partner or child or step-child under the age of 18
why_it_matters: A 20% shareholding threshold and any family trust are enough to make a counterparty entity an Associate, so booking the collar or the loan away from the individual does not avoid the policy.

clause: A clearance expires five (5) business days from its date, unless it specifies a different expiry date. ... Restricted Employees must confirm in writing to the Relevant Notification Officer, within three (3) business days of the dealing in Medibank Securities, the number of Medibank Securities affected and the relevant parties to the dealing.
why_it_matters: Any permitted leg must be executed within 5 business days of clearance and the bank's identity as counterparty must be disclosed to the company within 3 business days, since 'the relevant parties to the dealing' must be reported.

clause: Other Designated Persons must not ... use Company securities as security for loans, including for hedging and margin loan arrangements unless prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer.
why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies this one does not ban secured financing outright but gates it on a single prior written approval, so the loan leg of a funded collar is available in principle to Directors and other Designated Persons.

clause: lender disposals – a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights where prior written approval was received for entry into the arrangement, is excluded from the operation of this Policy.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement or physical settlement sale is excluded from the Policy, including during a Closed Period, provided the collar and loan were approved up front, which removes the usual fatal forced-sale risk.

clause: A member of the Company's key management personnel, or a Connected Party of such a member, must not enter into an arrangement which would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that has not vested or remains subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: For KMP the collar can only be written over shares that have both vested and come off any holding lock, and no approval can cure a collar over unvested or locked remuneration.

topic: drafting gap for KMP on vested shares
clause: The approval-gated bullets on limiting economic risk and using securities as loan security are addressed to 'Other Designated Persons', while the preceding paragraph addresses key management personnel only in respect of unvested or holding-locked remuneration.
why_it_matters: There is no express rule permitting or prohibiting a KMP hedging or pledging fully vested unrestricted shares, so a bank should require the Clearance Officer's written approval and, ideally, a Board confirmation of the reading.

clause: Designated Persons must not deal in Company securities on ... a speculative basis (including short selling).
why_it_matters: A written call and purchased put must be documented as risk management over a long-held position rather than a speculative or short position, and the collar should be delta-neutral rather than net short.

clause: a short-term basis (ie buying and selling within 3 months)
why_it_matters: The collar tenor and any unwind or roll should sit outside a three-month buy-and-sell pattern in the underlying shares, and shares recently acquired should not be collared and delivered within three months.

clause: Closed Periods run from the end of the financial year, half year, September quarter and March quarter until the first trading day after release of the corresponding results or quarterly report.
why_it_matters: MinRes has four blackouts a year because of quarterly reporting, so the windows for pricing and executing the collar and any roll are materially narrower than at a half-yearly reporter.

clause: The Clearance Officer ... may revoke their approval at any time. An approved dealing must occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective.
why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of the collar must complete inside five business days of clearance, and the bank bears the risk that clearance is revoked before signing.

clause: The Clearance Officer ... may in their discretion grant or refuse the request, or impose conditions on the dealing.
why_it_matters: Approval for the collar may come with conditions such as tenor, strike levels, disclosure or a maximum proportion of the holding, which must be capable of being reflected in the confirmation and loan documents.

clause: Dealings that would not satisfy the Front Page Test should not occur, even where the dealing may not strictly be prohibited under this Policy or otherwise at law.
why_it_matters: An anti-avoidance overlay that can defeat a technically compliant collar on reputational grounds, so the structure should be capable of clean public description and, for Directors, of Appendix 3Y disclosure.

clause: Personnel must not deal in the Company's securities, or in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities, during a Closed Period (unless exceptional circumstances apply).
why_it_matters: Entry, unwind, roll and cash settlement of the OTC options are themselves barred in Closed Periods for everyone, not just Designated Persons, absent an exceptional-circumstances approval.

clause: Designated Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Parties only deal in securities in circumstances where the Designated Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust, controlled company or superannuation fund does not avoid the approval and clearance requirements.

clause: Designated Persons must immediately notify the Company Secretary of any dealings in the Company's securities when any such dealings occur.
why_it_matters: Entry into the collar must be reported to the Company Secretary immediately and, for Directors, will feed a Listing Rule 3.19A Appendix 3Y disclosure of the change in the nature of their interest.

clause: pre-determined investment or divestment plans – dealings under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided by the Board and ... the plan cannot be cancelled during a Closed Period except in exceptional circumstances.
why_it_matters: Offers an alternative route: physical settlement of the collar could be structured as a Board-cleared non-discretionary plan so settlement is not blocked by a Closed Period.

clause: Meridian Restricted Persons may not enter into or continue with any margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Meridian Securities or in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.
why_it_matters: The second limb catches any loan secured on Meridian Securities, so the funded leg of a collar is prohibited for every director, executive and LTI participant, with no approval route.

clause: may not enter into or continue with any margin loan arrangements
why_it_matters: The ban is not merely prospective, so an existing secured facility must be unwound rather than grandfathered, and a person becoming a Restricted Person must exit any such arrangement.

clause: This restriction applies whether the Meridian Securities are held: in the name of the Meridian Restricted Person; or in the name of their spouses or partners or dependent children; or by trusts of which the Meridian Restricted Person is a trustee; or by any company which a Meridian Restricted Person controls.
why_it_matters: Routing the secured borrowing through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the prohibition.

clause: Where Meridian Persons are entitled to participate in any equity-based remuneration scheme, they must not enter into any transaction for any 'Associated Product' ... any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme.
why_it_matters: An absolute, approval-proof ban on the option legs to the extent they hedge scheme entitlements; it turns on eligibility under the scheme rather than on vesting, so the safest collar covers only shares acquired independently of any plan.

clause: Meridian Restricted Persons remain subject to this policy and will be deemed to be Meridian Restricted Persons for six months after their departure from Meridian.
why_it_matters: A retiring director or executive cannot put on a funded collar for six months after leaving, so the bank must diligence departure dates rather than current office.

topic: loan itself may be a security
clause: Security is defined broadly and includes any interest in, or right to participate in, any capital, assets, earnings, royalties, or other property of any person, and any interest in, or right to be paid, money that is, or is to be deposited with, lent to, or otherwise owing by, any person.
why_it_matters: On its face the definition sweeps in debt claims, so the loan and the OTC option confirmations could themselves be characterised as securities under the Policy, reinforcing that every leg needs General Counsel approval.

clause: must complete the approved trade within 10 trading days from the date of notification ... trading is still prohibited if a Meridian Restricted Person who has secured approval either has, or learns of, material information which is not generally available to the market. In those circumstances, the approval is automatically deemed to be withdrawn.
why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the option legs must complete within 10 trading days (2 trading days if approved for a Blackout Period), and the approval evaporates automatically if material information arises before signing.

clause: In the case of proposed trading by a director or the Chief Executive, the form must be signed by the Chair or, in the Chair's absence, the Deputy Chair and in the case of proposed trading by the Chair, the form must be signed by the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.
why_it_matters: Board-level sign-off, not merely a General Counsel tick, is needed before a director or the Chief Executive can execute any leg, which lengthens the lead time inside the 10 trading day window.

clause: any other period that Meridian's General Counsel specifies from time to time in relation to Meridian Securities
why_it_matters: Unannounced blackouts can be imposed on all or specified Restricted Persons at any time, blocking entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement of the structure.

topic: no incentive plan carve-out from short term rule
clause: Meridian Persons must not engage in short term trading (i.e. acquiring and then selling Meridian Securities within a three month period).
why_it_matters: Unlike most policies there is no exemption for selling shares received on vesting, so shares acquired within three months should not be delivered into a collar settlement.

clause: It also applies to companies, trusts and other entities controlled by any Meridian Person and any family member or other person acting on the direction or recommendation of a Meridian Person.
why_it_matters: The counterparty to the collar cannot be a family trust or controlled entity used to sidestep the approval and margin loan rules, as those entities are themselves bound.

clause: This is because the terms of such a loan may require the sale of Meridian Securities during a Blackout Period or while the Meridian Restricted Person is in possession of inside information.
why_it_matters: Meridian's objection is to lender-driven forced sales, so an unfunded collar with cash settlement and no security interest is the structure most likely to be approvable; the Policy contains no forced-sale carve-out.

clause: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons must obtain prior written approval for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending or securities lending arrangement, including ... the grant of a mortgage, charge, lien or other encumbrance or third party interest over the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: Ramsay gates rather than bans secured financing, so the loan leg of a funded collar and the security over the collared shares are both available on a single prior written approval from the Approving Officer.

clause: Sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale is excluded from the blackout, short-term and pre-approval rules, so lender enforcement does not put the executive in breach; the carve-out is not limited to margin lending.

clause: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons must not, without prior written approval, hedge Company securities.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs are permitted on approval rather than banned, and the Policy does not carve unvested plan securities out of that approval route, which is unusually permissive.

clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 12 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: The single biggest constraint on tenor: the collar should run well beyond 12 months and should not be documented as, or economically equivalent to, a short-dated forward, since forward contracts are the Policy's own example of a prohibited short-term dealing.

clause: Sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4 of this Policy do not apply to: ...
why_it_matters: The excluded dealings list is expressed only against the blackout, short-term and pre-approval sections, so the margin loan, encumbrance and hedging approvals in 5.7 and 5.8 continue to apply to everything, including plan dealings and non-discretionary plans.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: A collar cannot be documented around the rules; if its economic effect is a short position, a short-dated forward or an unapproved hedge, it will be treated as one.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: An express reputational veto over the hedging and secured financing approvals, so the structure must be capable of clean public description and Appendix 3Y-style disclosure.

clause: the duration of the approval will be 5 business days ... The approval to deal can be withdrawn at any time by the Approving Officer in his/her absolute discretion without giving any reason ... it is recommended that Restricted Persons apply for approval to deal at least 2 business days prior to the intended date of dealing.
why_it_matters: Pricing and execution must complete within five business days of approval, with two business days of lead time, and the bank bears the risk of unexplained withdrawal before signing.

clause: The Approving Officer may direct the person who is proposing to deal in the Company's securities not to deal, or impose conditions on the dealing in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons for any direction or condition.
why_it_matters: Approval for the collar may carry unexplained conditions on tenor, size, strikes or disclosure that the confirmation and loan documents must accommodate.

clause: The Procedures provide further guidance around who is a Restricted Person and a Connected Person.
why_it_matters: The perimeter of the approval regime, and who counts as a Connected Person for a family trust or controlled company, is set by an internal document the bank has not seen and should request.

clause: selling securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan requires prior written approval.
why_it_matters: A voluntary sale by the executive to meet a call needs fresh approval and may fall in a blackout, whereas a sale by the lender exercising its rights is excluded, so the facility should rely on lender enforcement rather than borrower top-up sales.

clause: Any person who breaches this Policy could face disciplinary action (including forfeiture of securities and/or suspension or termination of employment).
why_it_matters: Forfeiture of plan securities is an express sanction, which would strip collateral out of the structure if the arrangement is later found non-compliant.

clause: trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Employee or a Connected Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a blackout period, the plan does not permit the Employee or a Connected Person to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a blackout period.
why_it_matters: Offers a route for physical settlement of the collar to occur without regard to blackout periods, if the settlement mechanics are pre-approved as a non-discretionary plan.

clause: Restricted Securities are Auckland Airport Ordinary Shares; debt securities issued to the public; and any other listed securities of Auckland Airport or its subsidiaries, and any listed derivatives (including futures contracts listed on an authorised futures exchange) in respect of Auckland Airport securities. 'Trade' includes buying or selling listed securities, or agreeing to do so.
why_it_matters: OTC options written by a bank are neither listed securities nor listed derivatives, so the collar legs sit outside the consent and blackout machinery altogether; the constraint is the insider trading law and the unvested associated products ban, not the Policy's trading rules.

clause: The Policy contains no prohibition on, or consent requirement for, margin lending, pledging or any other secured financing over Auckland Airport securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is not caught by anything in the Policy, which is the single most permissive feature for a funded collar in this batch.

clause: The additional trading restriction for Restricted Persons does not apply to ... a disposal of Restricted Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: Lender enforcement, including during a blackout period, is expressly outside the Restricted Person restrictions, so the bank's security can be enforced without putting the executive in breach.

topic: associated products ban limited to unvested
clause: Where you are entitled to participate in any equity based remuneration scheme, you may not enter into any transaction for any associated product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any unvested entitlement you are eligible for under that remuneration scheme.
why_it_matters: The only absolute hedging ban, and it stops at vesting, so the collar must be confined to vested shares but is unconstrained once entitlements have vested.

clause: You should not engage in short term trading (the buying or selling of listed securities within a one month period), unless there are exceptional circumstances ... approved by General Counsel and one of the Chief Executive or the Chief Financial Officer.
why_it_matters: A short window compared with market practice, and it is framed around buying or selling listed securities, so it constrains delivery of recently acquired shares into a settlement rather than the tenor of the OTC legs themselves.

clause: A consent is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after notification. A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of material information prior to trading. ... where the trade is to occur during a blackout period, within [2] trading days.
why_it_matters: Any listed leg or share delivery must complete within 10 trading days of consent (2 during a blackout), and the consent evaporates automatically if material information arises before execution.

clause: In the case of proposed trading by a Director, the Request for Consent form must be signed by the Chair or, in his or her absence, the Deputy Chair and in the case of proposed trading by the Chair, the Request for Consent form must be signed by any other Director.
why_it_matters: Board-level sign-off is needed for any consented trade by a Director, so the share-delivery legs of the structure require more lead time than a management approval.

clause: Employees and directors will be considered responsible for the actions of trusts and companies controlled by them. In this respect, 'control' is not to be construed in a technical way but by looking at how decisions are made in practice.
why_it_matters: A family trust or investment company used as the collar counterparty entity is itself a Restricted Person, judged on practical rather than formal control, so it cannot be used to sidestep consent or blackout periods.

clause: The Board may approve updates, amendments to and exemptions to this policy from time to time, which may be implemented by written notice to you and/or posting on Auckland Airport's intranet.
why_it_matters: A general Board exemption power exists, so bespoke relief can be sought for the structure, but the same power means the permissive gaps in the Policy can be closed by notice at any time, including after the collar is in place.

clause: The rules contained in this policy do not replace your legal obligations. ... Sometimes behaviour that you consider to be ethical actually may be insider trading. If in doubt, don't!
why_it_matters: The Policy has no substance-over-form clause and no front page test, so the gaps are real, but this residual warning and the New Zealand insider trading law remain the operative constraints on entering the structure.

clause: the Restricted Person must comply with any disclosure obligations that person has under the Securities Markets (Disclosure of Relevant Interests by Directors and Officers) Regulations and the listing rules of any relevant stock exchange.
why_it_matters: Even though the Policy does not regulate the collar, the New Zealand relevant-interest regime is likely to require a director or officer to disclose the change in the nature of their interest arising from the security and the option legs.

clause: Restricted Officers and their Close Associates are prohibited from ... entering into any financial arrangements whereby a security interest is granted in respect of any vested VCX Securities which remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition.
why_it_matters: The prohibition on granting security is deliberately confined to vested-but-restricted securities, so a security interest over freely held vested securities is not prohibited, which is what makes a funded collar arguable at Vicinity.

clause: entering into arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements in relation to VCX securities, which may include entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of VCX securities, transferring VCX securities into an existing margin loan account and selling VCX securities held in an existing margin loan account.
why_it_matters: 'Properly described as margin lending arrangements' is narrower than a general secured financing ban, so a bilateral term loan with a fixed advance and no maintenance margin is arguably outside it, but the facility must be structured and documented so it is not in substance a margin loan.

clause: VCX securities: Any Securities of Vicinity Centres and any derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any VCX securities.
why_it_matters: The put and call written by the bank are themselves VCX securities, so entry, roll, unwind and settlement each require the dual approvals and must fall outside a blackout period.

topic: hedging ban tied to remuneration status
clause: hedging or entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition
why_it_matters: The collar may only be written over securities that have vested and are free of any trading restriction or forfeiture condition, so the bank must diligence clawback and holding-lock terms in the plan documents, not just vesting.

clause: The section 7 exclusions from the blackout restrictions cover only plan option exercises, takeover acceptances and transfers out of the employee share plan trust with no change in beneficial ownership.
why_it_matters: Unlike Ramsay or MinRes, Vicinity has no exclusion for a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights, so enforcement or physical settlement during a blackout period would be an unexcused dealing and a Policy breach.

clause: short-term dealing (i.e. if a person buys (or sells) VCX securities on a date and then sells (or buys) any VCX securities on a date that is less than 30 days after the first dealing)
why_it_matters: The test compares any two dealings in any VCX securities, and derivatives count, so the option legs and any share dealing must be spaced at least 30 days apart and settlement must not follow a recent acquisition.

clause: Chairman – approval from both the Chairman of the Audit Committee and the CEO; Other Directors – both the Chairman of the Board and the CEO; CEO – both the Chairman of the Board and the Chief Legal, Risk & ESG Officer or Group Company Secretary; All other Restricted Officers – any two of the CEO, Chief Legal, Risk & ESG Officer or the Group Company Secretary.
why_it_matters: Two approvers are required for every leg, which lengthens lead time and means the structure must be explained to Board-level approvers before pricing.

clause: A written response to a trading request should be given within two business days of the initial request. Trading by a Restricted Officer may be conducted no more than five business days after the trading request has been approved. ... Any trading request can be approved or not approved without giving reasons and can be withdrawn by email if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: Pricing and execution must complete within five business days of approval, and approval can be withdrawn by email at any point before the trade, which the bank must accommodate as a condition precedent.

clause: A decision not to approve a trading request is final and binding on the individual seeking approval. A refusal to approve a trading request is confidential information and must not be disclosed to anyone.
why_it_matters: There is no appeal, and the executive cannot tell the bank why a leg has been blocked, so the documents should not require the client to explain a refusal.

clause: the intention of this Policy not only to minimise the risk of insider trading but also to avoid the appearance of insider trading and the significant reputational damage that may cause
why_it_matters: Approval turns partly on appearances, so a collar over a large proportion of a director's holding is likely to be refused even where technically permitted.

clause: Any trustee of a trust or other fiduciary arrangement under which the Restricted Officer, their spouse or partner or their dependent children, are or may be a beneficiary; and any company in which the Restricted Officer, or any of the above-mentioned persons, directly or indirectly holds a majority of the shares or otherwise controls or significantly influences.
why_it_matters: The 'may be a beneficiary' and 'significantly influences' limbs are wide, so almost any family holding vehicle used as borrower or collar counterparty is itself bound by the section 8 prohibitions and the approval regime.

clause: Vicinity, Vicinity Centres or the Group means the stapled group of Vicinity Limited and Vicinity Centres Trust, of which Vicinity Centres RE Ltd is the responsible entity; 'securities' includes any unit or other interest in the scheme.
why_it_matters: The underlying is a stapled security comprising a share and a trust unit, so the collar confirmations and the security documents must describe the stapled security correctly and deal with a possible destapling.

clause: This Policy also applies to employees on extended leave from Vicinity, including parental leave, personal leave, long service leave, a career break or leave without pay.
why_it_matters: Time away from the business does not suspend the approval requirements or the section 8 prohibitions for the life of the collar.

clause: Derivatives has the meaning given in the Corporations Act, and includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Securities: put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.
why_it_matters: Both collar legs are expressly within the defined term with no venue limit, so section 7 governs the structure directly: banned over unvested securities, permitted over vested ones.

clause: Company Personnel and their Connected Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company's Securities, provided any Trading complies with the balance of this policy.
why_it_matters: This is a rare affirmative permission for hedging vested shares, so the derivative legs of a funded collar are contemplated rather than merely unprohibited.

clause: Designated Personnel or their Connected Person are prohibited from entering into margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company's Securities.
why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to margin loans strictly so called; a bank facility secured on the collared shares with margin or top-up mechanics is likely an 'arrangement in respect of Company's Securities' and would need to be structured, and confirmed with the Company Secretary, to sit outside it.

clause: The policy contains no prohibition on pledging, charging or otherwise encumbering Company Securities other than section 8 on margin loans, and no disclosure obligation for encumbrances.
why_it_matters: A non-margin term loan secured on the collared shares is not caught by any express prohibition, which is the key point of difference from policies that ban all secured financing.

clause: This includes buying and selling Securities within a six month period, and entering into other short term Trading (e.g. forward contracts).
why_it_matters: The collar tenor should comfortably exceed six months and should not be documented as a forward, or it risks being characterised as speculative short term Trading.

clause: Designated Personnel ... are prohibited from Trading ... outside of the following periods: a period of one month commencing on the business day after the day full year results are announced; ... half year results ...; ... the Company's annual general meeting.
why_it_matters: Entry, roll, unwind and any physical settlement of the collar must each fall inside one of only three one-month windows a year, and there is no exceptional-circumstances relief for anything other than a sale.

clause: The policy is silent on sales effected by a third party such as a lender, on margin calls and on price triggers.
why_it_matters: Neither excused nor declared a breach: lender enforcement or cash-settlement outside a window is unregulated by the text but would sit uneasily with the window regime, so the facility should avoid discretionary lender sales.

clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances surrounding the Company, could the proposed dealing be perceived by the market as the Company Personnel or their Connected Persons taking advantage of their position in an inappropriate way? ... Any Trade in Company Securities ... must not be made if that Trade would fail the 'front page' test.
why_it_matters: An open-textured veto that sits above the express permissions, so the Chair or Managing Director can decline a collar on reputational grounds even where every specific rule is satisfied.

clause: This policy also applies to the Connected Persons of the Company Personnel ... or a company, trust or entity that the person or any of their Connected Persons controls.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the margin lending ban, the trading windows or the notice requirement.

clause: It is recognised that in exceptional circumstances, a Designated Personnel or their Connected Persons may need to sell the Company's Securities outside of an Approved Trading Period. ... A clearance is valid for seven business days from the date of the notification and can be withdrawn if there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: The only out-of-window relief is for a sale, so an urgent collar unwind or restructure outside a window has no sanctioned route.

topic: grant of any rights to lenders
clause: Directors and Restricted Employees must not, and must ensure their Associates do not, enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any The Lottery Corporation Securities, or grant lenders any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities.
why_it_matters: The second limb is a flat ban on giving a financier any rights over the shares, which defeats the secured loan leg of a funded collar regardless of vesting state, loan purpose or loan-to-value ratio.
